routes.label: Locate the cut at the folded center and reflect its edge across both folds

question:
A square piece of paper is folded twice into four equal quarters, as shown below, then cut along the dashed line. When unfolded, the paper will match which of the following figures?

[Figure 1](figures/2023_AMC_8_Q02_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
The cut removes the corner where the two folds meet. That corner, marked \(B\) below, was the center of the original square, so the cut makes an interior hole while leaving the outside edges intact.

Start with the cut folded quarter:

[Figure 7](figures/2023_AMC_8_Q02_solution_folded_original.svg)

Unfolding reflects the cut across a fold. Opening the first fold turns the cut corner into a triangular notch along the still-folded edge:

[Figure 8](figures/2023_AMC_8_Q02_solution_one_unfold_original.svg)

Opening the second fold reflects that notch to its other side, joining four slanted cut edges into a diamond-shaped hole:

[Figure 9](figures/2023_AMC_8_Q02_solution_two_unfolds_original.svg)

The dashed lines track the fold axes; \(B\) marks where their meeting point was before the cut. The outside boundary is a square and the hole is a diamond, matching choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).

For a folded-paper cut, locate the cut relative to the folds first, then reflect it once for each unfold.
